message.content:
**Kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

| What you want | How to do it |
|---------------|--------------|
| **Terminate all running VS Code windows** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` |
| **Terminate a specific instance (by PID)** | `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` |
| **Terminate the process *and* all its child processes** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |

### Quick‑start

```cmd
:: Find the PID(s) of VS Code (optional)
tasklist | findstr code.exe

:: Kill all VS Code processes immediately
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

### Explanation

- `/IM code.exe` – matches the image name (`code.exe`) of the VS Code process.
- `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “kill -9” on Unix).
- `/T` – also terminates any child processes spawned by the target (useful if extensions spawn background tasks).

> **Caution:** This will close VS Code without prompting to save any unsaved files. Make sure you’ve saved your work before running the command.

### Alternative (PowerShell)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force
```

That’s all you need to force‑close VS Code from the command line!
